reviews.text:
I have a chipmunk, and its limbs and body have become bald. I went to another vet, but they didn't do anything to treat it. I heard good things about Earth Animal Hospital and decided to go there. Just as everyone else has said, they were very caring, carefully considering the medication and treatment options, and prescribed the right medicine.

I wish I had gone there sooner.

The doctor and staff were all very kind and explained how to administer the medication thoroughly.

It's truly a wonderful hospital.

My dog ​​🐶 wasn't feeling well, so I took him to the hospital.
They said he needed emergency surgery, and they treated him immediately.
Now he's running around happily. I'm so grateful to everyone at the hospital. …

Having welcomed my first dog as an adult, I started using this clinic because it's easily accessible from my home. Although I haven't been going there for very long, I feel confident entrusting my dog ​​to their care.

I've visited for vaccinations, checkups, and puppy parties, and the doctors, nurses, and reception staff are all warm and genuinely fond of animals. My dog ​​dislikes vaccinations and nail trims, but they praise him profusely when he cooperates, and I appreciate their kind words like, "You've grown so big!" and "You did so well!"

As a first-time dog owner, I have many questions about vaccinations and preventative care. While researching online reveals various opinions and can be confusing, the doctors explain the different options and risks, allowing my family and I to make informed decisions.

They treat both dogs and their owners with care and respect, and I hope to continue using their services in the future.

My sugar glider's condition suddenly worsened, and I urgently sought treatment at this hospital.

It was already in a critical state, and I was distraught, but the doctor explained the situation very carefully and provided the best possible treatment. The staff were also incredibly kind and helpful.

My sugar glider passed away that evening, but I am deeply grateful for their compassionate care until the very end.

And thank you so much for the flowers you sent later. Your unexpected thoughtfulness warmed my heart even amidst my grief.

I believe this is a truly wonderful hospital where you can entrust your beloved family member with peace of mind.

Thank you so much, doctor and staff.

I used to take my exotic animals here for checkups. The hospital itself isn't very big, but there are several examination rooms, and the doctors and receptionists are all very efficient and kind.

There's parking for about three cars in front of the hospital. There's a second parking lot, but it's a bit far away, so it might be a little inconvenient on rainy days. The consultation fees are reasonable, and if it were closer, I would have liked to take my dogs there too.

I've been a patient here for three years now, and I'm so grateful to the director and nurses. I started receiving care right at the beginning of the year, and now I'm healthy and free from nasal discharge and hair loss. Last year, the hair loss period was really tough, so I'm incredibly grateful to the doctor and nurses. I look forward to your continued support. 🐇🙇

I visited your clinic for a check-up for my guinea pig.

I was truly impressed by the wonderful service I received from Dr. Terayama, the receptionist, and all the staff at the hospital.

It's difficult to find a hospital that treats small animals like guinea pigs, and I decided to visit Earth Clinic after seeing positive reviews about their excellent service. I'm so glad I chose Earth Clinic.

I felt very safe in many ways, such as when the staff picked up my guinea pig while sitting on the floor, anticipating the risk of it falling, rather than holding it while standing.

Also, I was very surprised by how affordable the fees were. I had taken my rabbit to various hospitals, and the prices were usually double, so I really appreciate the reasonable pricing.

Thanks to you, the injury healed completely. I will be coming back for regular check-ups, so thank you in advance.

My hamster had diarrhea, so I took him to the hospital. They provided IV drips and medication, and they handled it well. Since he was so small, I was prepared for it, but it was gone by the time I next visited.

Later, I received some very cute and beautiful fresh flowers in the mail. I was surprised to receive flowers for a hamster. I think this hospital really values ​​the lives of animals.

Thank you very much. I'm happy to have such wonderful exotic animals nearby.

I was referred to this clinic by my older sister.
My sister had treated her rabbit here.
She was worried about the complicated surgery. The rabbit itself was elderly at 8 years old, but the director performed the surgery, which was a successful success and the rabbit is now healthy.

I used to rely on Dr. Sakamoto often, and he performed an emergency C-section on my degu.
It's been over two years since the surgery, and the degu is still in great health.
The doctors and staff are both polite and kind.
I feel comfortable visiting this clinic for dogs, cats, and other small animals.

However, I thought they might not be specialized in birds.
I've taken my bird there before, but it didn't get better, so we went to an avian specialist hospital and it got better there.
The diagnosis was incorrect, so I think it's best to take your bird to an avian specialist hospital.

A few years ago, I had my hamster examined by the director.
I recently passed by, so I'm writing this nostalgic review.

He underwent surgery here for a ruptured uterus, and thankfully made a full recovery. Unfortunately, he later developed quadriplegia and then rheumatoid arthritis, for which he was given medication.
By the way, he lived for a year after the surgery.
Thank you so much.

He always provided thorough explanations and various treatment options, and the director was very personable, which made me feel very at ease despite my anxiety.

He often had panic attacks in his carrier for visits to the hospital, but he would calm down when held, so I would secretly hide him in my clothes and hold him in the waiting room until my appointment. I was so grateful that he didn't mind examining him even though he was dirty and sweaty from his sticky hands.

Also, as a panic-prone hamster, I appreciated the fact that you can pay the after-hours fee to be seen earlier.

I'm sure Hamster had a terrible time with his illness, but thanks to this hospital we were able to see him off while easing his pain. I'm really glad we were able to take care of him until the very end.

I entrusted my beloved cat to this clinic for 11 years, from six months old.

The head veterinarian and all the staff were incredibly kind and attentive.

After her spaying surgery, she received annual checkups and vaccinations, and remained healthy for 10 years without any illnesses.

Last year, she developed acute diabetes and also suffered a brain disorder, leading to several life-threatening situations and repeated hospitalizations.

Managing her blood sugar levels was considerably more difficult than for a typical diabetic cat, but she bravely fought the illness for a year.

Until the very end, the doctors never gave up and did everything they could to treat her.

They patiently and thoroughly explained everything, addressing all my questions and concerns without showing any displeasure.

I was very worried about the amount of insulin I had to administer daily due to her unstable blood sugar levels, but they provided support not only by phone but also via LINE.

While some comments mention excessively high costs or insufficient explanations, I received thorough explanations from the beginning and am incredibly grateful for their support throughout my 11 years of visits.

They treated my cat as a cherished member of my family, always offering treatment options and medication choices that allowed me to consider my options as well.


They treated her with genuine care and consideration, always offering various treatment plans and medications. They considered ways to avoid unnecessarily high costs and to minimize the burden on my beloved cat.

Even so, veterinary bills for animals can easily be expensive.

My cat developed diabetes, and managing her blood sugar with injections, medication, special diet, IV fluids, and other miscellaneous expenses amounted to a considerable sum.

Therefore, I recommend getting pet insurance while your pet is still healthy.

My beloved cat was cared for by the vet's side until the very end, even during breaks, and passed away peacefully in her sleep.

I was sobbing uncontrollably that day that they told me, "You can pay the hospital bill later, once you've calmed down..."

Later, a beautiful bouquet of flowers arrived from the hospital.

Even now, three weeks after her passing, the flowers are still there, though they're slowly fading.

Thank you so much for 11 years of sincere and dedicated care. (⋆ᴗ͈ˬᴗ͈)”

My rabbit stopped eating, so I was worried and took him here for a checkup.

The doctor was kind and generally answered all my questions and concerns politely. He was also gentle and courteous with my rabbit. He seemed to be familiar with handling and handling rabbits. While I was waiting in the waiting room, many other small animal patients (birds, hamsters, chinchillas, rabbits, etc.) came in.

In the end, the cause wasn't clear, but they treated it as if that was the cause. I waited at home for a few days, and he recovered, so that was fine, but when I asked about the cost, their explanation was a bit vague. They were like, "Probably about this much?" On the other hand, if they told me that, I'd be well past my limit, right? I thought. It would be nice if they could tell me in advance on their website how much treatment would cost for a rabbit, so I could prepare myself.

Even though the initial consultation was the same, I was surprised to see that the charges varied depending on the doctor, as some charges were made this time that weren't there last time, and others were not. It seemed like they were just trying to take whatever money they could.

So that's how much it actually cost.

What particularly bothered me was that I was shocked when I entered the examination room, touched my rabbit's body without any explanation, and was suddenly charged 19,000 yen for the screening test. No treatment had been performed yet.

There are only a few hospitals that treat rabbits, and I'm sure fees are a concern, so I hope this information will be helpful for anyone considering taking their rabbit for a checkup. The doctor was kind and polite, and I was surprised that the initial consultation didn't cost this much at other hospitals either.

Both the receptionist and the clinic director were very polite throughout. If you make an appointment, they'll see you relatively quickly. There were two parking spaces in front of the hospital. They also asked about my symptoms over the phone in advance and gave me advice on what to do. If you are concerned, it is important to call and explain your symptoms in detail.

If your cat is a precious member of your family, I would recommend taking her to another hospital.
They do not provide loving care to animals who cannot express themselves in words.
My beloved female cat, who was almost 6 years old, was given unnecessary IV drips at this hospital, which caused her to develop ascites and she passed away 5 days after her visit.
There are many reviews, so please read them carefully and think carefully.
For me, this visit left me with nothing but an extremely painful experience that I will never regret.
If you are taking your precious family member to see a doctor, I would recommend taking them to another hospital.

This is definitely not a hospital I would recommend as a place to entrust the life of a beloved family member.

If you are hesitant, please do not consider taking your pet there lightly.

For me, this hospital left me with deep regrets.

I took my cat (5 years old) there for cystitis.

Although it wasn't a serious condition and was described as a typical case of cystitis, in addition to injections, a large amount of IV fluids were administered.

A few days later, her condition rapidly deteriorated, and ultimately, fluid accumulated in her heart and lungs, and she passed away.

Furthermore, despite the announcement that nighttime consultations begin at 8 PM, my visit at 7:30 PM was treated as a nighttime consultation, and I was treated without sufficient explanation.

Even though it was described as just cystitis, the bill for injections and IV fluids was approximately 40,000 yen.

I don't believe I received a satisfactory explanation regarding the treatment, the amount of IV fluids, the risks, the costs, or the classification of the consultation.

As can be seen in other reviews,
I believe it's true that many pet owners share similar distrust regarding the treatment, costs, and explanations provided. As a result of my own experience of losing a young life, I couldn't help but have strong doubts and anxieties:
"Was the medical care truly prioritizing the animal's life?"

Or was excessive treatment and medication becoming commonplace?

I hope that no other pet owners or animals will ever have to go through the same experience.
She's a kind teacher who will answer your calls even in the middle of the night.

My cat underwent surgery for urinary tract stones, but there was medical malpractice when the ureter was ruptured during catheter insertion. The hospital stay was prolonged, and when we argued about the surgery and other costs, the police were called, and I was threatened with "blocking the bladder again if you don't pay." I reluctantly paid the full treatment costs. My beloved cat is recovering well six months after the surgery, and I am grateful for that. I just wanted to share this experience here.
I had my rabbit examined. It was an elderly rabbit and its first visit, but the vet provided a thorough explanation and treatment. Thank you very much.
My beloved pet died here after surgery.
I took my dog ​​there. They gave him a thorough examination, and the staff were very kind!

I visited this veterinary clinic for my guinea pig's first check-up, and I was very pleased with the atmosphere, the doctor's and nurses' service, and the overall experience. I felt completely at ease leaving my pet there. This time, I had their nails trimmed and a health check-up, but I would definitely like to use this clinic again if needed in the future!

They also spoke kindly to my guinea pig throughout the visit, which was very reassuring.

I would definitely recommend this veterinary clinic.
Rabies vaccine and nail trimming cost 500 yen.

I continued to see this doctor for a while, even after the female doctor who could treat chinchillas retired.

When I went without an appointment because my chinchilla had epilepsy, the receptionist made it unclear whether they would even examine him, which left me feeling uncomfortable and anxious.

During the examination, I mentioned his strong breath and asked if he had mouth ulcers, but both doctors diagnosed it as soy milk fermentation.

I thought that couldn't be the case, so I found another hospital and had him examined.
The mouth ulcers had worsened significantly, and they removed his molars that same day.
Because he hadn't been able to eat, he developed hypertrophy, and it was almost too late.

If they can no longer treat chinchillas, I would like them to remove him from their list of animal care providers.

It almost cost my chinchilla his life.

I had my male cat neutered here.

Both the receptionist and the doctor were very kind and attentive, and I felt completely at ease entrusting my cat to their care.

I will definitely be using their services again in the future.

Thank you very much.

I visited the clinic several times.

During my first visit, instead of a definitive diagnosis, I was prescribed …
I went for a second opinion. The doctor who saw me explained everything thoroughly, including the medications prescribed by my regular doctor, which put my mind at ease. …

I went to this clinic because I heard they had a veterinarian who was knowledgeable about rabbits, but I was shocked by the terrible veterinarian (male).
After receiving an ultrasound, X-ray, and blood work and being explained the …

About six months ago, I underwent surgery for my ferret's intestinal blockage.
Before coming here, he had been examined three times elsewhere, but the problem was overlooked. …

I took my hamster to get checked for a suspected uterine prolapse, but they anesthetized her and performed an ultrasound without my knowledge, claiming the hamster was restless. Afterwards, they demanded over 23,000 yuan, which is extremely unreasonable. I suggest finding another clinic to avoid being scammed by unscrupulous operators.
I had my pet's surgery performed, and everything was fine until the procedure was completed successfully. …
